# Planned Scope for v2.1.0

**Status**: MCP adapter revision implemented; local verification complete, publication pending.

**Version sequence**: Implementation builds on the committed v2.0.0 source.
The optional add-ons are planned for the subsequent v2.1.0 release and do not expand the scope of
[v2.0.0](v2.0.0-scope.md). No publication date has been set.

This document is an upstream planning record for the original Delivery System
repository. Project templates under `docs/` remain generic.

## Goal

Provide optional MCP-backed adapters, packaged as add-ons, for connecting external delivery tools.
Users select an add-on and use its supplied AI prompt to adapt the integration
to their project and the external system.

Reusable instructions live under `addons/` at the repository root. `docs/`
remains reserved for the adopting project's actual content, decisions, and
workflows.

## Agreed Deliverables

- `addons/README.md` explains selection, use, adaptation, and removal of add-ons,
  including the boundary between instructions and active project configuration.
- The initial release includes add-ons for Jira, Confluence, GitHub Projects,
  and GitLab with this shared structure:

  ```text
  addons/
    README.md
    mcp-setup.md
    configure_mcp.py
    jira/
      README.md
      instructions.md
      mcp-setup.md
      integration-prompt.md
      deactivation-prompt.md
    confluence/
      README.md
      instructions.md
      mcp-setup.md
      integration-prompt.md
      deactivation-prompt.md
    github-projects/
      README.md
      instructions.md
      mcp-setup.md
      integration-prompt.md
      deactivation-prompt.md
    gitlab/
      README.md
      instructions.md
      mcp-setup.md
      integration-prompt.md
      deactivation-prompt.md
  ```

- Each `README.md` describes the purpose, prerequisites, scope, use, and removal
  of its integration.
- Each `instructions.md` defines setup and adaptation rules: authoritative
  sources, ownership, content and ID mapping, synchronization direction,
  conflict and failure handling, permissions, and permitted agent actions.
- Each `integration-prompt.md` provides a reusable AI prompt that examines the
  existing project, checks available interfaces and tools, resolves required
  decisions, and guides adaptation of the selected integration to that project.
- Each `deactivation-prompt.md` provides a copyable retirement workflow, including
  a remote/local knowledge inventory, an explicit user decision about migration
  or external retention, and verification of required migration before shutdown.
- The root README and general delivery guide link to the optional add-ons and
  explain how to remove individual add-ons or the entire directory.
- An adoption guide for existing v2.0.0 projects explains selective integration
  of the add-ons while preserving existing project content and rules.

## Constraints

- Add-ons are activated only through explicit selection. Their presence alone
  does not trigger external actions or changes to project rules.
- Preserve the context-dependent workflow introduced in v2.0.0: agents load
  only the instructions relevant to the selected integration.
- Preserve existing security, approval, and open-question gates. An integration
  prompt does not grant blanket authorization for external write operations.
- Setup checks existing project conventions and does not introduce a competing
  documentation or task structure without an explicit decision.
- Record project-specific decisions and durable working rules in the appropriate
  project locations. Once configured, active integrations must not depend on
  retaining the `addons/` directory.
- Do not store credentials or tokens in the repository. Document only required
  permissions and references to credential configuration.
- Users can remove unused add-ons or the entire `addons/` directory. Associated
  references must be cleaned up, and the core workflow must remain usable.
- Deleting instructions does not disable an established connection. Each add-on
  separately explains how to remove its active project integration.
- This release provides adapters with an executable project-client configuration
  helper, MCP setup, operation/identity contracts, and prompts. It does not ship a
  dedicated synchronization service or credentials. MCP authentication and actual
  target capabilities must be verified before claiming operation readiness.
- Tickets and their tasks require visible stable ID prefixes and verified native
  parent/child hierarchy. Links, checklists, boards, or unparented issue creation
  are not substitutes. Required update/hierarchy gaps block the selected workflow.
- Existing explicit external source-of-truth decisions must survive capability
  failures. A proxy adds transport compatibility, not missing server operations.

## Revised Adapter Requirement

The project owner clarified that these packages must operate as adapters, with
actual MCP setup, and that ticket/task nesting and unique ID names are mandatory.
This replaces the earlier instruction-only interpretation. See the
[adapter decision](v2.1.0-adapter-decision.md) for findings, chosen approach, and limits.

## Implementation and Ownership

Implementation follows the work on v2.0.0. The Technical Lead is the primary
owner of the shared integration structure and its compatibility with the
delivery workflow. The Content Editor supports instructions and prompts;
the Backend Developer and DevOps Engineer contribute on interface and access
questions. QA verifies the acceptance criteria.

Before implementation, review the then-current v2.0.0 rules and official
interface and tool documentation. Claims about product capabilities and tool
compatibility require verification against those sources.

## Acceptance Criteria for v2.1.0

- All four adapters provide product-specific MCP setup, usable prompts, and a
  shared executable config helper with scoped local tests.
- New configuration is previewed, preserves unrelated settings, and never stores
  literal credentials. Existing matching profiles are reused.
- Connection/authentication, current-session tools, target reads, and operational
  readiness are separately verified; no mapping-only activation is claimed.
- Native hierarchy, ID-prefixed titles, updates, and reciprocal read-back are
  capability gates before ticket creation. Unsupported workflows stay blocked.
- Setup is verified against both a new and an existing project, preserving
  existing documentation, IDs, project rules, and approval boundaries.
- For each project, prompts resolve the target system, authoritative sources,
  data mapping, synchronization scope, and permissions before dependent changes
  are made.
- Links, paths, and examples are consistent and verified. Claimed integration
  capabilities have supporting evidence; remaining verification limits are
  documented.
- The core workflow works without add-ons. Verify removal of unused instructions
  and removal after completed setup.
- Required project rules remain available after setup even when the `addons/`
  directory has been removed.
- Instructions clearly distinguish deleting add-on files from disabling an
  active integration.
- Adoption from v2.0.0 is optional and does not require restructuring existing
  project documentation.

See the [verification record](v2.1.0-verification.md) for completed checks and
runtime limits, and the [draft release notes](release-notes-v2.1.0.md) for the
prepared release summary.

## Authorization Status

The project owner subsequently authorized implementation of the agreed v2.1.0
scope and subsequently authorized committing and pushing it to the feature
branch for integration testing. Tagging and publication remain unauthorized. Implementation does not perform external setup
against a user's accounts or modify active project or agent rules.
